scope: Additional desktop Chromium 180-record reload experiment, separate from the stable forged-payload/CSV gate
observed: One reload preserved attempt ID/time/deadline/lock but lost attempt-start marker; the repeat passed. Another earlier trial reached the hidden unlock field but its driver timed out before normal five-tap reveal.
hypothesis: Interrupted native unload writes can select the persistence-integrity path; that path also used a last-119 slice and discarded origin markers. This cause is not proved for the recorded native failure.
remediation: Origin markers survive the integrity path. Two valid signed copies with a guard-only, non-weakening revision difference reconcile to the newer conservative state; identity/answers/deadline/joker differences or lock weakening still fail closed. Both MACs must validate. Controlled tests and the native E5 reload regression verify this; five post-fix native high-volume observations retained origin/deadline without integrity locks.
followup: E9 must broaden native reload/pending-write repeatability coverage; five favorable observations do not prove all browser/lifecycle cases.

followupObservations.interpretation: Origin retention is hardened; one native ordinary reload still blocked. Root cause and repeatability remain open.
